Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation Perspective for the Coefficient of Variation

Source: R/ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.Rd

Simulates a sample size plan for the coefficient of variation to show what it delivers when the population value differs from the planning value, or at a sample size chosen in advance. It takes the population coefficient of variation, either a planning value or a sample size, and a target width, and returns summaries of the estimate, the interval width, the proportion of intervals no wider than the target, and coverage over G simulated normal samples (Kelley, 2007; Maxwell, Delaney, & Kelley, 2027, Section 3.11 on power-based sample size planning).

Usage

ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity(
  true_cv = NULL,
  supposed_cv = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  assurance = NULL,
  true_mean = 100,
  specified_N = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_cv

Population coefficient of variation (the data generating value); a single positive number

supposed_cv

The supposed coefficient of variation, the planning value from which ss_aipe_cv plans the study (a value the researcher supposes, not an estimate computed from data); must be positive. Supply this or specified_N but not both.

width

Desired (full) width of the two-sided confidence interval for the population coefficient of variation; a single positive number. With specified_N it may be left NULL, and pct_ci_less_width is then NaN.

assurance

Probability with which the realized interval should be no wider than width, passed to ss_aipe_cv: NULL (plan for the expected width) or a single number strictly between 0 and 1; see ss_aipe_cv for how the procedure behaves near .50. With specified_N it is only echoed.

true_mean

Population mean used by the simulator to generate data, a single positive number (the standard deviation is determined by true_mean and true_cv, since CV = sigma/mu). Default 100.

specified_N

Pre-specified sample size to evaluate, a whole number of at least 4 (use this when you want the sensitivity results at a fixed N rather than at the N that ss_aipe_cv would recommend); incompatible with supposed_cv.

conf_level

Desired confidence level (i.e., 1 - Type I error rate); default 0.95

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications; defaults to 1000. Increase (e.g., 5000 or 10000) for stable Type I error estimates.

print_iter

Logical. If TRUE the simulation prints the iteration index after each replication (helpful for long runs); default FALSE.

filename

An optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the two confidence limits, the realized coefficient of variation, a coverage indicator, and the interval width): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the run reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with columns term and value summarizing the Monte Carlo results across the G replications. The term entries are: "mean_cv", "median_cv", "sd_cv" (mean / median / SD of the observed sample coefficients of variation); "mean_ci_width", "median_ci_width", "sd_ci_width" (corresponding summaries of the realized interval widths); "pct_ci_less_width" (proportion of intervals at or below the planning width width); "pct_ci_miss_low" and "pct_ci_miss_high" (tail-specific non-coverage); "total_type_I_error" (overall empirical non-coverage of true_cv); plus the input echoes "total_N" (the sample size evaluated), "true_cv", "supposed_cv" (NA when specified_N was supplied instead), "width", "conf_level", and "assurance" (present only when an assurance was supplied). The proportion rows are on the 0 to 1 scale, not percentages, so total_type_I_error is the sum of pct_ci_miss_low and pct_ci_miss_high.

Which replications each row describes. Three rules decide it.

  1. A replication whose sample mean is not positive has no confidence interval for the coefficient of variation (ci_cv requires a positive mean), and its sample coefficient is negative or undefined; this can happen when true_cv is large and the sample is small. All ten statistic rows, mean_cv, median_cv, and sd_cv included, describe the replications with a positive mean, so that every row is about the same samples. Such a replication is recorded with its coefficient and missing limits in the file filename names. One warning of class dmar_replications_without_interval states how many there were, and the count is attr(, "simulation")$failed.

  2. An interval can have an infinite upper limit (see ci_cv). Such an interval has infinite width and counts as not meeting the width target in pct_ci_less_width. mean_ci_width and sd_ci_width are over the finite widths, since one infinite width would make both uninformative, and median_ci_width is over all widths, infinite ones included. The number of infinite widths is attr(, "simulation")$n_infinite_width.

  3. An interval with an infinite upper limit is a valid interval of ci_cv, which signals nothing for it. One warning of class dmar_replications_with_infinite_limit states how many replications had one and how they enter the rows; the condition carries the count as n_replications and the number of replications as G.

The attribute simulation (see the section on the record of the simulation) has one element more here, n_infinite_width.

Details

Sample size planning for the coefficient of variation under the Accuracy in Parameter Estimation framework chooses N so that the expected (or, with assurance, the high-probability) confidence interval width is no larger than width (Kelley, 2007). Because the procedure assumes the planning value supposed_cv matches the population value true_cv, in practice the realized width will deviate from the planned width whenever the planning value is wrong. This sensitivity analysis quantifies the deviation by Monte Carlo simulation: the planned N is obtained from ss_aipe_cv with supposed_cv, then samples are drawn from the true population (with coefficient of variation true_cv) and the realized confidence interval widths are summarized.

For planning a sample size so that a confidence interval is sufficiently narrow, see Maxwell, Delaney, & Kelley (2027, Section 3.9.1.5, and Section 4.9 on assurance).

The samples are drawn from a normal population, which the interval and the plan assume, so the function does not show what a plan delivers for a population that is not normal. With a skewed population the coverage of the interval departs from the stated level: in 40,000 samples at each of the three plans for a coefficient of variation of .50, a width of .20, and 95 percent confidence (79 without assurance, 97 with an assurance of .80, and 142 with .99), coverage was .97 for a gamma population with that coefficient of variation, and for a lognormal one it was .915, .913, and .905, lowest at the largest plan. The proportion of intervals no wider than width was .55, .88, and 1.00 for the gamma population and .59, .84, and .99 for the lognormal one. For a normal population that probability, computed from the noncentral t distribution, is .53, .84, and 1.00 (see ss_aipe_cv and ci_cv).

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Chattopadhyay, B., & Kelley, K. (2016). Estimation of the coefficient of variation with minimum risk: A sequential method for minimizing sampling error and study cost. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 51(5), 627–648. doi:10.1080/00273171.2016.1203279

Kelley, K. (2007). Sample size planning for the coefficient of variation from the accuracy in parameter estimation approach. Behavior Research Methods, 39(4), 755–766. doi:10.3758/BF03192966

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapter 3 on confidence intervals for effect sizes.)

See also

ss_aipe_cv, ci_cv, cv

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Textbook scenario (Kelley, 2007). A researcher plans a study to estimate the
# coefficient of variation of reaction times with a 95% confidence interval no
# wider than .10. They guess from prior work that the population coefficient of
# variation is around .25 and apply ss_aipe_cv() to obtain a planned N.

# Question 1: how does the realized interval width behave when the planning
# value is correct (well-specified case)? G = 100 keeps the example quick;
# a reported sensitivity analysis deserves the default G = 1000 or more.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity(
  true_cv          = .25,
  supposed_cv      = .25,
  width            = .10,
  assurance        = NULL,
  conf_level       = .95,
  G                = 100,
  print_iter       = FALSE
)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_cv            0.246
#>  median_cv          0.245
#>  sd_cv              0.021
#>  mean_ci_width      0.098
#>  median_ci_width    0.098
#>  sd_ci_width        0.009
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.590
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.010
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.010
#>  total_type_I_error 0.020
#>  total_N            59   
#>  true_cv            0.250
#>  supposed_cv        0.250
#>  width              0.100
#>  conf_level         0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 100
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# Question 2: what happens if the planning value is materially smaller than
# the true coefficient of variation (a common direction of misspecification,
# since planning values are often optimistic)? The intervals will be wider on
# average than the target and the pct_ci_less_width will fall.
set.seed(113)
ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity(
  true_cv          = .35,
  supposed_cv      = .25,
  width            = .10,
  assurance        = NULL,
  conf_level       = .95,
  G                = 100,
  print_iter       = FALSE
)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_cv            0.343
#>  median_cv          0.343
#>  sd_cv              0.030
#>  mean_ci_width      0.145
#>  median_ci_width    0.144
#>  sd_ci_width        0.015
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.000
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.010
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.010
#>  total_type_I_error 0.020
#>  total_N            59   
#>  true_cv            0.350
#>  supposed_cv        0.250
#>  width              0.100
#>  conf_level         0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 100
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
